detail:
The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) describes depression, also called major depression, major depressive disorder, or clinical depression, as a mood disorder that is different from ordinary sadness. NIMH notes it can cause severe symptoms that affect how a person feels, thinks, and handles daily activities such as sleeping, eating, and working, and that it can affect anyone. Research cited by the institute suggests genetic, biological, environmental, and psychological factors all play a role.

NIMH describes major depression as including symptoms of depressed mood or loss of interest most of the time for at least 2 weeks that interfere with daily activities, and persistent depressive disorder as a less severe form lasting much longer, usually at least 2 years. Signs and symptoms can include persistent sad or empty mood, feelings of hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and changes in sleep and appetite. Clinicians diagnose depression from the pattern, duration, and effect of symptoms, and NIMH describes treatment as typically involving psychotherapy, medication, or both.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about depression symptoms and treatment options.
summary: NIMH describes depression as a mood disorder distinct from ordinary sadness, with major depression defined by symptoms most of the time for at least 2 weeks that interfere with daily activities, and treatment typically involving psychotherapy, medication, or both.

title: Depression: a mood disorder beyond ordinary sadness
